interest: Covers Japanese intelligence and British/French diplomacy in Indochina, including Allied debate over Mountbatten-backed French sabotage operations.
overview: This State Department decimal file (894.20251G, File 1479) documents intelligence, espionage, and covert military activities involving Japan and Allied countermeasures in French Indochina between March 1941 and December 1944. The file begins with early wartime cross-reference sheets concerning Japanese subversive efforts—specifically a Domei News Agency representative acting as an undercover agent—and intercepted radio communications transmitted by J. Edgar Hoover's Department of Justice. The remainder of the file comprises a secret November 1944 Office of Strategic Services (OSS) memorandum identifying the relocation of the Japanese espionage and liaison headquarters in Indochina from Hué to Tourane (Da Nang), as well as two December 1944 memoranda of conversation between Secretary of State Edward R. Stettinius, Jr., and British Ambassador Lord Halifax regarding Lord Mountbatten's proposal to deploy French personnel for sabotage operations in Indochina, a matter held for the personal decision of President Franklin D. Roosevelt.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a military attaché report regarding a Domei News Agency representative in French Indochina suspected of conducting subversive activities for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference (1941): a Domei News correspondent in Indochina, 'Ata', suspected of acting as a Japanese agent undermining French authority.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Domei News Representative in Indo-China

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording the Department of Justice's transmission of intercepted radio messages and translations concerning Japanese activities.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a 1942 Hoover letter transmitting intercepted Japanese radio messages, filed under 862.20294/42.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Intercepted Japanese Radio Messages

subfiles.about: Secret OSS intelligence memorandum reporting the transfer of the Japanese Liaison Headquarters and espionage base in French Indochina from Hué to Tourane.
subfiles.from: Bernard A. Towell (Office of Strategic Services)
subfiles.summary: OSS memo: Japan's liaison bureau with Vichy authorities moved from Hué to Tourane, serving mainly as an espionage cover.
subfiles.title: OSS Memorandum on Japanese Espionage Headquarters in French Indo-China

subfiles.about: Memorandum of conversation between Secretary of State Stettinius and British Ambassador Lord Halifax concerning British inquiries on sabotage activities in French Indochina.
subfiles.from: Edward R. Stettinius, Jr. (Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Stettinius tells Halifax the US will soon answer Britain's pending query on sabotage activities in French Indochina.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation between Stettinius and Halifax on Sabotage in French Indo-China

subfiles.about: Memorandum of conversation detailing British requests for presidential approval to attach French personnel to Lord Mountbatten's headquarters for sabotage operations in Indochina.
subfiles.from: Edward R. Stettinius, Jr. (Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Stettinius tells Halifax that Mountbatten's plan to attach French personnel for Indochina sabotage awaits President Roosevelt's decision.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation between Stettinius and Halifax on Mountbatten's Sabotage Operations in Indo-China
